title: Celestis Systems - integrated refarch & marketplace connector sync

Connector packaging (container images, helm charts, SBOM)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jared (Celestis), Aisha (Celestis), Ben (Celestis), Sara (Celestis)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood, I'm the account lead. Quick roll call?
[00:09] Jared: Jared here - Head of Platform at Celestis.
[00:12] Aisha: Aisha, cloud arch, hi.
[00:14] Ben: Ben - security and compliance.
[00:16] Sara: Sara - product.
[00:18] Liam: Liam O'Connor, solutions engineering on the Redwood side.
[00:21] Maya: Cool. Agenda — we want to align on the marketplace connector packaging and the reference architecture for private deployments, plus security artifacts and pilot acceptance criteria. Any additions?
[00:30] Jared: Sounds right. We also want to confirm metering/billing hooks — how usage shows up in marketplace versus our own billing.
[00:36] Ben: And I need to understand the KMS/HSM story and SBOM for container images.
[00:41] Liam: Great, we'll go through an architecture sketch then packaging expectations, then security. I'll share my screen with the reference diagram in a sec — apologies if the auto-transcription messes up redwood product names.
[00:52] [screen share starts — brief pause]
[01:10] Liam: Ok, topology 1 is hosted with VPC peering — Redwood control plane remains in our cloud, connector runs in Celestis VPC as a small deployment that proxies requests to dedicated inference pools. The key parts: signed container image, helm chart, serviceaccount RBAC, and an optional sidecar for metrics export to Prometheus.
[01:34] Aisha: For us peering is doable but we have bastion plus strict egress rules. The connector needs to work behind a proxy and only talk outbound on 443 to a specific IP set.
[01:45] Liam: Yep, we can support outbound-only connections, we use a persistent TLS connection with mutual auth for private deployments. We'll need the IP ranges or DNS allowlist — that'll be on the packaging checklist.
[01:56] Maya: Quick note — for marketplace listing we also need a packaged offering that can be deployed via a helm chart or an ARM/CloudFormation reference for cloud marketplaces, plus a short listing manifest.
[02:07] Sara: How opinionated is the helm chart? We run a few clusters with different CNI and pod security policies.
[02:13] Liam: We try to keep values.yaml flexible: image repo, resource requests/limits, nodeSelectors, tolerations, and proxy env. We also provide a minimal manifest for air-gapped installs — that needs customers to bring an image pull mechanism or private registry.
[02:27] Ben: About SBOM — what format do you provide? SPDX? CycloneDX? We need something we can ingest into our scanner.
[02:34] Liam: We generate a CycloneDX SBOM and can also provide SPDX on request. Signed image and container signature via cosign, and we can provide the cosign public key for verification.
[02:44] Ben: Good. Also, KMS: do you support customer-managed CMEK in cloud providers or require Redwood KMS?
[02:50] Maya: We have options. For Redwood Private deployments customers can integrate with their KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer bring-your-key for model cache encryption and logs; for hosted there's a customer-managed encryption option for data at rest in some plans. We'll follow up with specifics.
[03:06] Jared: For the listing, marketplace policies force some required metadata — license, support SLA, and data residency statements. Can you provide a sample listing text?
[03:15] Maya: Yes, we'll share a template that includes required fields and suggested verbiage for support tiers — we'll also include our pricing metering endpoints for usage metering.
[03:24] Aisha: We need to validate network egress pattern during our security review. Is there a way to simulate traffic so we can audit connections?
[03:31] Liam: We can provide a staging connector that points to a sandbox endpoint with verbose logging for a week-long soak test. That should let you capture flows and firewall hits.
[03:40] Ben: Firewall logs are crucial. Also we need assurance on audit logs from the connector and optionally on request tracing tied back to the customer's SSO identity.
[03:48] Liam: Connector emits structured logs and metrics and supports OpenTelemetry traces. For identity mapping we recommend using OIDC claims forwarding — we can surface the bearer identity in the headers if you want.
[03:57] Sara: On acceptance criteria for the pilot, what are the minimum tests? Latency, correctness, availability?
[04:03] Maya: From Redwood's side we propose: 1) successful end-to-end inference with your sample dataset, 2) meeting a p95 latency target under your expected QPS, 3) logs and metrics flowing to your stack, and 4) security signoffs: SBOM, signed image, KMS notes.
[04:19] Jared: We'll add automated regression prompt sets to check output quality.
[04:24] Liam: Perfect. Back to packaging — marketplace often wants a deployable artifact and an ops runbook. We have a runbook template we can plug into the listing.
[04:33] Aisha: For air-gapped installs, can you confirm how much disk/ephemeral storage the connector needs? Some of our clusters have very small root volumes.
[04:41] Liam: Minimal footprint is ~1 vCPU and 1.5GB RAM for the connector container in a lightweight mode; with local caching and additional components that might go up to 4 vCPU/8GB. We'll include sizing guidance.
[04:55] Ben: On compliance, do you have a SOC2 report we can reference? Also, penetration test cadence?
[05:01] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II report for the control plane and can provide a redacted version under NDA. We do quarterly pentests and can share summary findings and mitigation tracking.
[05:12] Ben: We may need a signed attestation for specific controls for our procurement team.
[05:16] Maya: Understood, we'll route that through legal and send a draft attestation.
[05:20] [short pause]
[05:28] Liam: Quick question — Celestis mentioned potential on-prem connector variations. We typically publish two reference architectures: 1) VPC-peering/proxy outbound, 2) fully air-gapped with image import and no outbound, with a synchronous batch upload pattern. Which are you targeting?
[05:46] Aisha: We're primarily VPC with proxy, but we want the air-gapped pattern as a stretch for regulated customers.
[05:53] Liam: Ok we'll supply both diagrams and a checklist for air-gap steps (image bundle, credentials exchange, offline license file, local model cache initialization).
[06:05] Sara: Regarding billing hooks — does the connector call a metering endpoint or do you rely on server-side metrics from Redwood to reconcile usage?
[06:12] Maya: Marketplace listings usually require a metering URI that records usage events; we can either emit usage pings from the connector (signed) or rely on server-side token accounting. The recommended pattern is server-side records plus a reconcile file for the marketplace.
[06:27] Jared: We'll want reconciliation so our finance team can map charges to internal orgs.
[06:32] Maya: Noted. We'll include a reconciliation sample CSV and the mapping fields you should expect.
[06:37] Ben: A small point on RBAC — can we ensure the connector respects least privilege? For example read-only serviceaccount for logs.
[06:44] Liam: Absolutely — our helm values include RBAC toggles and we document minimal permissions. We'll show a sample policy.
[06:51] [10 minute mark - checking recording timestamp may drift]
[10:05] Aisha: I'd like to walk through the actual helm values quickly, if Liam can post the sample.
[10:11] Liam: I'm pasting a repo link in the chat — it's a staging repo: https://git.redwood-demo/staging/celestis-connector (note: placeholder). Key values: image.repo, image.tag, proxy.endpoint, metrics.enabled, otel.collector.url, resources.requests.cpu, resources.requests.memory, nodeSelector, tolerations.
[10:34] Aisha: Great, for our cluster we will set tolerations and nodeSelector to use private nodes.
[10:39] Liam: Also note a flag 'airgap.enabled' that toggles offline mode, which removes imagePullSecrets and expects local tarball import.
[10:47] Sara: On the marketplace listing side, what's the expected review window? We have internal SLOs for publishing new listings.
[10:53] Maya: Marketplace reviews vary by cloud but typically 5-10 business days once the package and documentation are submitted — we'll coordinate to hit your timelines.
[11:03] Jared: Our timeline is we want a pilot starting Oct 19 and production by early November if all goes well. Is that feasible?
[11:10] Maya: Yes that aligns — we'll prioritize the packaging checklist for week of Oct 4 and schedule the UAT workshop for the week of Oct 12.
[11:19] Ben: On legal, procurement will ask for indemnity and SLA language; can you surface standard terms for marketplace offers?
[11:26] Maya: We'll include a standard marketplace terms packet and flag any enterprise-only clauses. Legal PR will follow up.
[11:33] Liam: Slight digression — if you want to run micro-benchmarks against our dedicated pool we can provide a small qps/lantency harness and access to a staging endpoint. That helps set expectations for p95.
[11:45] Aisha: Yes please, micro-benchmarks would be helpful for capacity planning.
[11:48] Liam: We'll attach a harness and sample scripts.
[11:52] [14 minute mark? timestamps get loose here — transcript has natural drift]
[14:05] Sara: Are there any known blockers for marketplace certification on your side? For example specific signing or naming conventions?
[14:12] Liam: Main blockers are signed images and SBOMs, ensuring the helm chart passes linting, and providing a minimal security questionnaire. We have templates for each.
[14:22] Ben: For the security questionnaire, can you pre-populate answers? That speeds review.
[14:26] Maya: Yes, we'll send a pre-filled draft for your review.
[14:30] Jared: Ok, to be clear on deliverables: we expect from Redwood — packaging checklist, helm repo, SBOM, cosign key, runbook, sample reconciliation CSV, and UAT schedule. From Celestis — VPC CIDRs, firewall rules, list of clusters for pilot, and procurement/legal contacts.
[14:49] Maya: That's a good capture, I'll put those in action items.
[14:54] Liam: One more technical: do you plan to run model-serving inside your environment or always call Redwood hosted pools?
[15:01] Aisha: We prefer hosted pools for core inference but want the option to run a lightweight model runtime for specific regulated datasets.
[15:08] Liam: Ok we can support both — the lighter runtime is included in the air-gapped bundle as an optional field, but note that model licensing and quantization requirements differ. We'll include notes on supported ops and quantized builds.
[15:19] Ben: For the pilot acceptance we'll also want a security checklist signoff item — maybe a short meeting with your security engineer.
[15:25] Maya: We'll coordinate that — likely under NDA.
[15:29] Sara: Any competitor differentiators we should highlight for procurement?
[15:33] Maya: Briefly — our focus is production inference economics: predictable latency, caching/batching controls, and a unified API across deployment modes. We also provide first-class eval tooling to catch quality regressions.
[15:46] Jared: Good. That helps with the internal narrative.
[15:50] [wrap-up section]
[15:52] Maya: Recap and explicit next steps: we'll share the packaging checklist and helm repo by Oct 4, Liam will push the sample helm chart to staging by Oct 8, and we schedule the UAT/runbook workshop for week of Oct 12. Celestis will share VPC CIDRs and procurement contacts by Oct 6.
[16:10] Aisha: Sounds good.
[16:12] Ben: I'll follow up on the SOC2 NDA request.
[16:15] Sara: We'll get the pilot cluster list together.
[16:18] Jared: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clear checklist.
[16:21] Maya: Thanks all — we'll send notes and links after this call.
[16:25] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcription: speakers overlap occasionally and some technical terms were mis-transcribed (helm chart repo link is a placeholder). The team should rely on the artifacts we attach rather than this raw transcript for exact config snippets.
